replacements.old: - [ ] Formalize the task-relevant representation problem using established Information Bottleneck / rate-distortion terminology where applicable.
replacements.new: - [x] Formalize the task-relevant representation problem using established Information Bottleneck / rate-distortion terminology where applicable. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae4-information-bottleneck-v1` IB-1: `L_beta(T) = I(T;X) − beta·I(T;Y)` minimised over **all 4140** deterministic encoders of an 8-atom support, with a machine-readable crosswalk of **6** entries each carrying a citation — the bottleneck itself (Tishby, Pereira & Bialek 1999, arXiv:physics/0004057), its deterministic hard-partition variant (Strouse & Schwab 2017, doi:10.1162/NECO_a_00961), rate-distortion (Shannon 1959; Cover & Thomas 2006), minimal sufficient statistics (Lehmann & Scheffé 1950, doi:10.1214/aoms/1177729695), decisions and actions (Tishby & Polani 2011, doi:10.1007/978-1-4419-1452-1_19) and rational inattention (Sims 2003, doi:10.1016/S0304-3932(03)00029-1). The scope restriction is a checked receipt field, not an implication: `stochastic_encoders_optimised: false`. Every entropy is an exact rational combination of prime logarithms and **no logarithm is ever evaluated** — `H(Y)` for the AND world is reported as `2*log2(2) − 3/4*log2(3)`.

replacements.old: - [ ] Determine when a GMI minimal behavioral/predictive state is equivalent to, refines, or is incomparable with an IB-optimal representation.
replacements.new: - [x] Determine when a GMI minimal behavioral/predictive state is equivalent to, refines, or is incomparable with an IB-optimal representation. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae4-information-bottleneck-v1` IB-2: the relation is classified at **every** point of a 9-point exact rational tradeoff ladder for **7** registered worlds. Two of the four relations occur — `EQUAL` **44** times and `GMI_STRICTLY_REFINES` **41** — and the other two are exactly **0** and are reported as such. The answer is a threshold, not a hedge: `T_GMI` becomes IB-optimal at `beta = 1` for six worlds and only at `beta = 6` for the exactly rational noisy channel, because a channel caps `I(T;Y)` strictly below `H(Y)` so the full predictive state has to be weighted far more heavily before it pays for its own description. Below the threshold the optimum is a **strict coarsening** of `T_GMI`.

replacements.old: - [ ] Prove smallest counterexamples preventing unqualified identification.
replacements.new: - [x] Prove smallest counterexamples preventing unqualified identification. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae4-information-bottleneck-v1` IB-3: the smallest support carrying a counterexample at a **non-degenerate** tradeoff is **2**, witnessed by the registered channel `(0, 1/4)` at `beta = 1`, where `T_GMI = 01` and the IB optimum is the one-block encoder `00`; minimality holds because support size 1 is vacuous, so every strictly smaller size is exhausted by construction. Separately, the **stronger** counterexample kind — an IB optimum *incomparable* with `T_GMI` — is shown **not to exist** at this scope: **0** instances over support sizes 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 searched exhaustively across all partitions, all deterministic targets and the whole ladder, and **0** over the registered 8-atom worlds. That negative is kept, labelled `EARNED_BY_EXHAUSTION`, and the general statement is recorded as a **conjecture**, not a theorem.

replacements.new: - [x] Distinguish `retain information about Y` from `retain information required for action/control under utility U`. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae4-information-bottleneck-v1` IB-4: within a fixed capacity class the encoder carrying strictly **more** information about `Y` — strictly smaller `H(Y|T)`, compared by the exact prime-log sign test — is strictly **worse** for control value under the registered utility in **162,242** encoder pairs, and the ordering **reverses** in **280,779**. replacements.new: - [x] Derive conditions under which forgetting task-irrelevant information is optimal under resource constraints. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae4-information-bottleneck-v1` IB-5: merging two atoms costs no relevant information **iff** they carry the same conditional law `p(Y|x)`, while capacity `I(T;X)` strictly falls — so under any capacity constraint the merge is optimal. The full-versus-blind probe has `VoI = 9/64` over a cost increment of `7`, break-even `9/448`: strictly below it the fine sensor wins (`85/128` vs `71/128`), **at** it the two are exactly tied (`71/128` vs `71/128`) — the tie is reported, not skipped — and strictly above it the blind sensor wins (`57/128` vs `71/128`).

replacements.new: - [x] Prove that observational compression/prediction does not generally identify causal structure. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-1: over the complete census of **547,625** SCMs — all **25** labelled DAGs on three binary variables, every CPT drawn from the frozen grid `{0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1}` — the 25 DAGs fall into **11** Markov equivalence classes, and **all 7** classes containing more than one DAG carry an exhibited witness: two parameterisations of **different** DAGs whose observational joints agree on **all 8 atoms** as exact rationals and whose interventional answers differ. **80,788,144** such cross-DAG disagreeing pairs exist over **26,601** joints realised by two or more DAGs of one class. The quantifier is kept: the **4** singleton classes **are** identified, and they are reported with count `0` rather than omitted — the claim is *not generally identified*, never *never identified*.

replacements.new: - [x] Construct observationally equivalent worlds with different intervention consequences. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-2: `A → C` against `C → A` with `B` isolated, `P(A=1) = 1/2`, `P(C=1|A=1) = 3/4`, `P(C=1|A=0) = 1/4`. The observational joint `(3/16, 1/16, 3/16, 1/16, 1/16, 3/16, 1/16, 3/16)` sums exactly to `1` and is reproduced by exactly **1** parameterisation of the other DAG, found by exhaustive search over the frozen grid. The registered answers then separate completely: `ACE_A_on_C` is `1/2` under one member and `0` under the other, `ACE_C_on_A` is `0` and `1/2` — the identification interval of each is the full `[0, 1/2]` while the observational joint is identical cell by cell.

replacements.new: - [x] Define when interventions are required for the behavioral specification. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-3: interventions are required for a specification `(query, tolerance)` **iff** the half-width of that query's identification interval over the observational equivalence class exceeds the tolerance. The rule is tested on both sides and **at** the boundary: with worst-case half-width `1/2`, at tolerance `31/64` interventions are required, at exactly `1/2` they are **not**, and at `33/64` they are not — the flip is verified at the exact rational threshold rather than sampled around it. Per query, **5,356** of **26,601** joint groups have a non-degenerate interval and **21,245** are identified observationally; the four registered queries give identical counts, as the relabelling symmetry of the full census forces.

The worst case over the census is `1/2`. Intervention is **not** universally worth its cost, and this is exhibited rather than conceded: **84,980** query-group specifications have value of intervention exactly `0`, and a named one is carried in the receipt — `ACE_C_on_A` on a joint realised by all **25** DAGs, identified answer `0`, interval width `0`.

replacements.new: - [x] Distinguish predictive state from causal/control state. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-5: on the registered confounded subfamily `B → A`, `B → C`, `A → C`, the predictive state (the partition of the four `(A,B)` contexts by `p(C=1|A,B)`) and the causal/control state (the partition by the full interventional response vector `(p(C=1|do(A=0)), p(C=1|do(A=1)))` at that context) are different objects: over the **2,187** strictly positive models (**75,938** excluded for a zero atom, reported not dropped) the relation is `INCOMPARABLE` **1,458** times, `PREDICTIVE_STRICTLY_REFINES` **486**, `EQUAL` **243**, and `CAUSAL_STRICTLY_REFINES` **0** — the last a **proved** zero, not an unobserved one: the causal state separates only the two values of the context, so for it to refine the predictive partition strictly the predictive partition would have to be trivial, and then the causal one is trivial too and the relation is `EQUAL`.

replacements.new: - [x] Relate to causal-state, causal-representation-learning and causal-inference parents precisely. — ✅ `gmi-833-ae-ae13-causality-intervention-v1` CI-6: **6** crosswalk entries, each with a citation — truncated factorisation and do-calculus (Pearl 1995, doi:10.1093/biomet/82.4.669; Pearl 2009, doi:10.1017/CBO9780511803161), Markov equivalence (Verma & Pearl 1990; Andersson, Madigan & Perlman 1997, doi:10.1214/aos/1031833662), partial identification (Balke & Pearl 1997, doi:10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074), experimental design (Hauser & Bühlmann 2014, doi:10.1111/rssb.12071), causal representation learning (Schölkopf et al. 2021, doi:10.1109/JPROC.2021.3058954) — with **3** `PARENT_SUFFICIENT` terminals recorded as successes. The entry that matters most is the sixth: the computational-mechanics `causal state` (Shalizi & Crutchfield 2001, doi:10.1023/A:1010388907793) is a **purely predictive** equivalence class of histories with no interventional content and is **not** the Pearlian causal structure; `COMPUTATIONAL_MECHANICS_CAUSAL_STATE_IS_PEARLIAN_CAUSAL_STATE` is a registered forbidden promotion and CI-5 measures how far apart the two notions actually sit.

lane_findings.subject: gmi-833-ab-terminology-harness-v1 repo-wide ratchet versus the #833 freeze standard
lane_findings.detail: The AB ratchet fails a PR when any NEW paper-facing .md carries a banned term. This lane removed every avoidable hit from its prose; 7 remain and ALL of them are inside committed FREEZE_V1.md files, which the #833 custody model forbids editing once results exist. Two of the seven are unavoidable in principle: one is a VERBATIM quotation of an issue row whose own text contains a banned term (the #833 standard requires that quotation to be byte-exact), and one is the literal on-disk path of a sibling package whose directory name contains the term. The remaining five are this lane's own prose inside AE4's freeze, avoidable only if the banned-term list is consulted BEFORE the freeze is written.
lane_findings.recommendation_for_the_orchestrator: either exempt FREEZE_V1.md from the paper-facing scope of the ratchet (a freeze is a custody document, not paper-facing prose), or add the verbatim-issue-row and sibling-package-path cases to the gate's exception mechanism. A research lane cannot fix this without editing another package's gate configuration or tampering with its own freeze.

lane_findings.subject: gmi-833-aa-ledger-gate-v1 repo-wide self-test versus debt already on main
lane_findings.detail: The ledger gate landed on main after this lane branched and requires every named result in a *THEOREMS*.md to emit assumptions, dependency, falsifier and strongest-parent ledgers. This lane merged main, found 20 of its own results non-compliant, and repaired all 20 -- the gate's owned-files check now reports 0 violations for AE4, AE7 and AE13. The job still fails, on a separate repo-wide self-test (real_repo_gate_green) whose only violations are 5 results in research/gmi-833-ag5-extension-lowering-v1/AG5_EXTENSION_THEOREMS_V1.md, merged into main by #1036. No path of this lane appears in that failure.
lane_findings.recommendation_for_the_orchestrator: the AG5 package needs the same four-ledger repair; until then the aa-ledger-gate job is red on every branch cut from main, exactly the shape #1032 fixed twice before for other gates.
